newsitem.title: FRANCE: Britain's GEC bids for Thomson-CSF stake.
newsitem.headline: Britain's GEC bids for Thomson-CSF stake.

text.p: Britain's GEC Plc, testing France's commitment to European defence cooperation, has made a bid for the state's controlling stake in defence electronics firm Thomson-CSF, a French rival said on Wednesday.
GEC and the French government declined comment, but French conglomerate Lagardere said it knew that GEC, its partner in an aerospace venture, had submitted a bid.
"We were aware of it. We didn't learn of it from the press," Noel Forgeard, managing director of Lagardere's defence unit Matra Defense Espace, told reporters.
"GEC is the second-largest European group in the businesses in which Thomson and Matra are involved so it's natural that it would leave a calling card in such a competition," he said.
Forgeard said his company did not consider the GEC move as "unfriendly" to its own bid.
Lagardere and engineering group Alcatel Alsthom -- both of whom have business partnerships with GEC -- said last Friday that they had put in separate bids for the stake.
The two competed last year during the proposed privatisation of the whole Thomson group, comprising Thomson-CSF and consumer electronics firm Thomson Multimedia (TMM).

The government originally said it preferred the offer from Lagardere, which planned to merge its missiles business with Thomson-CSF and sell TMM to Daewoo Electronics. But it cancelled the plan in December after an independent Privatisation Commission objected to the terms of the sale.
The commission's decision followed an outcry against the TMM sale to a Korean company for the symbolic sum of one franc.
The Finance Ministry recently announced plans to re-launch the privatisation, beginning with the sale of Thomson-CSF, which it indicated would be open to any European candidate.
Defence experts say French defence groups risk isolation unless France allows European competitors to take part in the restructuring launched by President Jacques Chirac last year.
The ministry had no comment on reports in three French dailies -- Le Figaro, La Tribune and Le Monde -- of a GEC bid.
Asked whether Lagardere and GEC might team up in the final stages of the bidding, Forgeard said he would not comment on his company's proposal until the final bids were submitted.
The government has until next Monday to declare which candidacies are valid. The bidders then have until May 7 to make final offers. France has said it will choose a buyer by June 30.
"The French government has difficulty hiding its embarrassment," Le Monde said.

It said GEC's candidacy was awkward because the government wanted to use the privatisation of Thomson-CSF to consolidate the domestic defence industry and thus ensure the French would be powerful players in a European industry restructuring.
Alcatel has teamed up with plane maker Dassault in its bid for Thomson-CSF. Dassault is due to merge with state-owned Aerospatiale, which the government barred from the bidding process.
Alcatel said it would start talks with Germany's Deutsche Aerospace and GEC Plc if it won the Thomson stake.
Alcatel is partners with GEC in the GEC Alsthom industrial power and high speed trains venture.
Lagardere also has wider European ambitions. It is allied with GEC in the GEC Marconi space business and has a missiles partnership with British Aerospace.
GEC Marconi has a joint sonar venture with Thomson-CSF.
Thomson-CSF shares closed up 1.95 percent at 188.50 while the French market finished down two percent.
